full_judgment:
3. The learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge) heard the said issue separately at the instance of the defendant and under misconception of law and facts passed the impugned order (Order No. 141 dated 1-11-76) holding that the learned Court has no jurisdiction to try the above suit and, as such, returned the plaint for filing in the proper court, meaning thereby the filing of the appeal in the court of the learned District Judge, Khulna under the provisions of East Pakistan Ordinance No. 1 of 1962. 

 4. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied thereby the plaintiffs preferred this revision alleging that the impugned order is illegal since the same has been passed on misconception of law and facts of the case. It is further alleged that the above suit having been filed in the year 1961 under the provision of Bengal Waqf Act, 1934 then in force challenging the ex parte decision illegally deciding the suit property as waqf property by the defendant No. 1 under section 46A of the said Act of 1934 is illegal and bad in law. 

 6. Heard Mr Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate for Mr Hasan Fowz Siddique, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, who submits that the learned Court below erred in law in returning/rejecting the plaint of the above suit on misconception of law and fact. He further submits that the court below had acted illegally and without jurisdiction in returning the plaint in failing to find that the action taken and legal proceeding instituted under the provision of the said Act of 1934 have been saved and protected under Chapter X of Ordinance I of 1962 and section 4 of the Ordinance No. XIII of 1966. The learned Advocate thereafter referred to section 6 of the General Clauses Act and the decisions in the case of Mohammad Bachal vs. Rehabilitation Commissioner, Hyderabad and another reported in PLD 1962 (WP) Karachi, 889 and Abu Sayed Rashid Majumder vs. Mukhtar Bari Majumder and another reported in 19 DLR 65 in support of his claim. 

 7. I have gone through the above rulings and reasons to believe that the facts and circumstances of the cases referred to above have got similarity with that of the present case on principle. It may be recalled here that the present suit was filed in the year 1961 when Bengal Waqf Act, 1934 was in force and the Waqf Ordinance /62 (I of 1962) came into force on 19-1-62 having no retrospective effect. So, as per law the instant suit is liable to be guided under the relevant law (Bengal Waqf Act, 1934) which was prevalent at that time. 

 9. Regard being had to the above provision of law I am led to hold that the learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge) committed wrong in disposing of the matter under Waqf Ordinance I of 1962. Further, the bonafide could be proved by examining witnesses to show as to whether suit property is waqf property or secular property which justify the petitioners' claim that they have been prejudiced since no opportunity was provided to prove the whole case. 

 10. All these facts and circumstances led me to hold that the learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge) committed illegality in passing the impugned order which led to miscarriage of justice. Since the impugned order is found illegal prima facie I don't like to enter into other points raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. In these circumstances, it is held that the impugned order suffers from material illegality and, as such, it cannot sustain.
